thread:
Maya: Quick kick — we have a condensed launch for MicroSeq (mini benchmark + webinar) and need a lightweight creative pack for paid, organic, and the webinar page. Deadline: everything final Apr 2 so web can go live Apr 4. Can design confirm scope + rough ETA?

Ravi: Scope check: what hero sizes + motion do you need, and are we doing A/B creative for messaging? Also do we need a data table graphic for the blog?

Maya: Yes on A/B hero (two messaging lines). Required outputs:
- Hero: 1920x1080 static PNG + H.264 MP4 loop (6s), lightweight 1280x720 MP4 for low bandwidth, and animated GIF (max 2MB) for email.
- Social pack: 1200x1200, 1200x628, 600x600. Each with 1x and 2x retina exports.
- Benchmark mini-card: SVG sparkline + PNG fallbacks (full-width 1200x300 and compact 600x150). Include an optional numeric caption frame for slide use.
- Data table graphic: A3/US Tabloid PNG + CSV for accessibility.
- Slide master: Google Slides + PPTX masters (title + data + speaker).
- Press-ready one-pager: PDF (A4 + US Letter), layered text.
- Component tokens: Figma library with color tokens, spacing, typographic scale, and an annotated example of the comparison component so PMs can swap model names.
- Localization: Prepare text layers for en/es/de; do not rasterize text.

Tess: Timing estimate: hero motion + static (2 days), social pack + retina (1 day), sparkline + CSV (0.5 day), slides + one-pager (1.5 days), figma tokens (0.5 day). If I start today I can post an initial pass Mar 29 and final Apr 1. Need final copy & headshots by Mar 27.

Maya: Good. Messaging: avoid absolutes ("fastest") per legal; use language like "optimized for low-latency inference" or "cost-efficient inference." Add link to methods page on publish.

Anya: Legal note: any comparative claim needs a citation to our benchmark methodology and the exact test harness. For landing/social we can use the tempered claims Maya suggested. If you want an explicit numeric claim (e.g., "25% lower latency"), send the test log and numbers to me.

Ravi: For the data table, do you want raw numbers or indexed values? Indexed will be simpler visually.

Maya: Use indexed sparkline (0-100) for the visual, with an optional hover/slide numeric frame that shows median latency (ms) and cost/1k tokens. Devon will provide the spreadsheet.

Devon: Spreadsheet incoming to Figma comments: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/xyz-microseq (I put the median & p95 cols). Also dropping small methodology blurb for the blog.

Tess: Figma link for designers: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/MicroSeq-mini-bench. Please upload headshots to the "assets/headshots" page.

Maya: Handoff checklist for dev: include export manifest + naming conventions and alt text. Also need a 16:9 low-bandwidth hero (1280x720) and a cropped mobile hero (820x360).

Tess: Will include an assets.json manifest and a dev-ready README. Example filenames I will export:

```
microseq_hero_v1_1920x1080.png
microseq_hero_v1_1920x1080_loop.mp4
microseq_hero_v1_1280x720.mp4
microseq_social_1200x1200_v1@2x.png
microseq_sparkline_v1.svg
microseq_sparkline_v1_fallback_1200x300.png
microseq_datacard_v1_1200x300.png
microseq_slidemaster_title_v1.pptx
microseq_onepager_v1.pdf
assets_manifest_v1.json
```

Tess: Export specs (short):
- MP4: H.264 baseline, target bitrate 2.5Mbps for 1920x1080, 1.0Mbps for 1280x720.
- GIF: maximum 2MB, looped 6s.
- PNGs: sRGB, 72dpi, 1x & 2x.
- SVG: use CSS variables for color tokens, include role/title/desc tags for accessibility.
- PDF: export PDF/X or PDF/A for press-ready, fonts embedded.

Maya: Brand tokens: use --redwood-500 for accent, reserve --redwood-700 only for CTA hover states. Ensure AA contrast for body text and large-scale headings meet AA. Add alt text to every export.

Anya: Quick copy guidance: replace any "lowest" or "best" phrasing. Suggested CTAs: "Register for the demo" / "See the mini-benchmark" / "Watch the MicroSeq walkthrough." I can approve final copy by Mar 30.

Devon: For inbound lead routing, ask growth if they want a hidden UTM param for A/B tracking. If yes, include both CTA variants in the manifest with UTM templates.

Maya: Growth confirmed — include utm_source=microseq&utm_campaign=spring-launch and add variant suffixes.

DesignBot: Automated export queued. Manifest URL (private): https://assets.redwood-inference.com/microseq-mini/manifest_v1.json

Ravi: One more ask from paid channel — we need PNG tiles with a 10% padded safe area for overlays and a transparent CTA badge as a separate PNG so ads can be localized without recrops.

Tess: Will add a CTA badge PNG with transparency and a safe-area export. Also adding a layered source PSD for the paid ops team.

Maya: Action items recap:
- Tess: initial creative pass Mar 29, final April 1 (all files in Figma + exported manifest).
- Devon: drop spreadsheet + headshots Mar 27.
- Anya: copy review and sign-off Mar 30.
- Ravi: confirm paid sizing and safe-area needs by EOD today.
- Growth: confirm UTM mapping (Devon noted confirmation).

Ravi: Confirmed on paid sizing & safe area.

Tess: Will post initial frames in this thread when available. :sparkles:

Maya: Appreciate it everyone — ping here if anything blocks. :rocket:
